A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same LoRA knowledge-memory study. Their main text, figures, tables, equations, and Appendices A–U can be matched reliably, and the added material in v4 is readable.

before.justification: v2 reports original capacity, synthetic-supervision, routing, merging, long-document QA, and latency experiments, plus appendix ablations.

after.justification: v4 retains these original results and adds routing comparisons, scaled-concatenation results, and evaluations on two additional long-context benchmarks.

M1.justification: Appendix O introduces an evaluated procedural variant, CAT-1/sqrt(N), which rescales both LoRA factors before concatenation. This is a limited adaptation within the existing composition framework; the principal LoRA training and TIES-based inference procedures remain.

E1.justification: v4 retains the original datasets and adds ∞Bench and LongBench v2 evaluations involving documents above 100K tokens, reaching 364K tokens. This substantially extends the input-length regime beyond the filtered 10K–20K NarrativeQA documents and 64K PhoneBook experiment in v2.

E2.justification: v4 adds Arrow, SpectR, and LAG as evaluated alternatives to embedding-based routing on NarrativeQA and QuALITY, at both Top-1 and Top-3 retrieval depths (Table 6). It also adds scaled CAT to the merging comparisons in Figures 7 and 20, substantially broadening comparison of the system's routing and composition components.

E3.justification: The additions introduce a CAT normalization control and new benchmark protocols: 20 ∞Bench documents evaluated with ROUGE-L and 30 LongBench v2 documents evaluated with accuracy, using Qwen3-8B and Qwen3-1.7B. The retained experiments' master configuration, training budgets, splits, and metrics remain unchanged.

E4.justification: v4 adds targeted follow-ups to Q9–Q10: testing whether routing limitations persist across router families and whether CAT's collapse stems from update magnitude rather than rank expansion. Existing layer/module, DoRA/PiSSA, merge-count, and Flash Attention analyses are retained.

E5.justification: Neither version reports experimental seed counts, repeated-run counts, confidence intervals, error bars, or significance tests. The added results continue the existing point-estimate reporting practice.

E6.justification: v4 adds substantial result blocks in Tables 6–7 and scaled-CAT entries in Figures 7 and 20. For example, the retained Llama vanilla-CAT score is 0.19, while the newly evaluated scaled variant scores 4.77, alongside retained Linear and TIES scores of 4.92 and 5.41. These are additional method results; the original main benchmark Table 2 remains numerically unchanged.

T1.justification: Appendix O adds explicit factor-averaging formulas and derivations contrasting CAT's summed update with the scaled variant's averaged update. This is a localized mathematical extension. The new BA expressions are inconsistent with the stated A dimensions of d by r and B dimensions of r by k.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same central contribution: an empirical audit of LoRA's capacity, supervision requirements, composition bottlenecks, and complementary role alongside ICL/RAG. The added experiments support these retained claims.

C2.justification: v2 attributes CAT's failure to rank expansion without alignment; v4 instead identifies scale mismatch as the dominant cause and interprets normalized concatenation as competitive with linear averaging. It also discusses persistent bottlenecks across router families and setting-dependent viability above 100K tokens. The overarching hybrid-memory interpretation and continual-update limitations remain.

D1.justification: v4 adds a code-and-dataset repository link in the abstract and clarifies that linear merging averages low-rank factors, alongside explicit scaled-CAT instructions. These improve access and implementation documentation without establishing that retained experiments were rerun. Existing hardware specifications, prompts, and training details remain.

R1.justification: v4 adds a brief discussion of hypernetwork-based adapter generation citing Text-to-LoRA, Doc-to-LoRA, and SHINE, plus references for SpectR and the new benchmarks. The broader positioning as a memory-focused empirical audit remains unchanged; repeated entries for previously cited works do not constitute new research coverage.

P1.justification: Changes include localized rewrites in Q9–Q10 and Appendices N, O, and Q, a short Impact Statement, and updated proceedings and affiliation text. The fifteen-question narrative and appendix organization are preserved.

P2.justification: v4 adds Tables 6–7, inserts scaled-CAT bars into Figures 7 and 20, expands Figure 8's timing caption, and reflows the document. Existing displays largely retain their organization and visual design.

improvement.justification: The scaled-CAT control improves the explanation of a failure that v2 attributed too broadly to concatenation, while additional router and extreme-context evaluations strengthen the empirical audit. The repository link also improves reproducibility information. These benefits outweigh the local dimension-order defect in the added algebra, but sparse documentation and absent uncertainty estimates for the new evaluations limit the overall gain.
